subject: SLA: downtime bucket / monthly credit proposal
messages:
From: Mark DeLuca <mark.deluca@harbortech.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@harbortech.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: SLA language for scheduled maintenance / credit buckets

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at HarborTech is working through the contract and we need to align on the availability language before we sign. Two items we want to discuss:

1) Standard uptime target — your template references 99.95% for hosted endpoints. Given our fenway-critical batch windows, we would like clarification on how scheduled maintenance windows are accounted for (are they excluded from the 30-day calculation?).

2) Monthly credit scale — the template has a single-bracket credit at 5% for <99.5%. We want either a more gradated band or an explicit "downtime bucket" carve that allows small routine maintenance bursts without triggering credits.

Can you share suggested redlines (or a short proposal) showing how Redwood would handle a quoted maintenance window per month (we expect a single 4-hour window for minor patching) and what the monthly credit would look like if availability dips below the floor?

I'm attaching HarborTech's standard redlines and the procurement checklist for reference. Emily (cc) will handle legal-level edits.

Thanks,
Mark

Subject: Re: SLA language for scheduled maintenance / credit buckets

Mark —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick take from our side so legal and procurement have something to work from:

- Baseline uptime: we typically propose 99.95% monthly for Hosted API endpoints.
- Scheduled maintenance: we exclude pre-announced maintenance windows where we give >=72 hours' notice. For your use case (single monthly 4-hour minor patch window), that would be excluded from the availability calculation provided the window is scheduled and does not exceed the agreed monthly maintenance allowance.
- Downtime bucket approach: instead of gradated credits based purely on thresholds, we can specify a monthly "maintenance allowance" (up to 8 hours/month) that is not counted as downtime. Only unplanned availability loss beyond that allowance contributes to credits.
- Credits: propose a two-tiered credit schedule instead of a single 5% band:
    * Availability >= 99.0% and < 99.5% -> 5% of monthly fees
    * Availability < 99.0% -> 15% of monthly fees

I'll attach a redlined SLA (SLA-template-v3.pdf) with the exact wording for the maintenance allowance and the calculation formula. I'm looping in Soojin (legal) and Marcus (serving/runtime) to confirm the operational feasibility and the exact phrasing so it holds up in audit.

Two quick questions for you:
1) Do you have a preferred definition for "pre-announced" (how many hours notice is required)?
2) Is HarborTech open to the 8-hour monthly allowance (we can flex down to 4 if you need) — we'll note the allowance in Appendix A.

I expect a short call could settle both items; happy to set one up this week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: SLA language for scheduled maintenance / credit buckets — operational note

Vanessa / Mark / Soojin —

A couple operational clarifications from infra so the wording maps cleanly to SLO telemetry:

- How we calculate availability: we compute successful request ratio across the tenant's production endpoints over the monthly window, excluding time ranges marked as "scheduled maintenance" in our incident system. The precise metric is (1 - (sum_unavailable_seconds / total_seconds_observed)) * 100.
- Scheduled maintenance tagging: to be excluded, a maintenance window must be created in the customer-facing maintenance calendar and accepted by both parties with >= 48 hours notice. We can accept 48 hours (instead of 72) if HarborTech needs faster cycles, but we'd like to keep 48 hours as a minimum for coordinated rollouts.
- Maintenance allowance: implementing an 8-hour allowance is straightforward; we track cumulative scheduled maintenance minutes per calendar month and exclude up to the allowance before counting downtime. Anything beyond the allowance is considered unplanned for the credit calculation.
- Edge cases: emergency security patches that require immediate action will be marked as "emergency maintenance" and are excluded by default but would prompt post-action notices. We recommend limiting emergency exclusions to CVSS >= 8.0 events to avoid overuse.

I'll attach an uptime visualization (Uptime-chart-Sept.png) to show an example month where scheduled maintenance consumed 4 hours and unplanned incidents consumed 22 minutes — under the allowance, so no credits were triggered.

If legal wants hard numeric language, propose the following clause for Appendix A (draft):

"Scheduled Maintenance Allowance — Redwood and HarborTech agree that up to eight (8) cumulative hours of pre-announced scheduled maintenance per billing month shall be excluded from the Monthly Availability calculation provided such windows are posted to the Maintenance Calendar with no less than forty-eight (48) hours' notice. Any scheduled maintenance exceeding the allowance will be treated as downtime for the purposes of the Monthly Availability calculation."

Happy to review precise redline language after Soojin/legal propose wording.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Vanessa / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the appendix language, Marcus — that helps a lot. A couple of small edits from HarborTech legal:

1) Notice window: HarborTech prefers 72 hours' notice for standard maintenance to match our change freeze policy (we can accept 48 hours only for emergency security patches). Would Redwood accept 72 hours as the default and carve out the 48-hour emergency path?

2) Credits: HarborTech is open to the two-tier schedule, but given our risk profile we're asking that the first credit band (Availability >=99.0% and <99.5%) be 7% rather than 5%. The second band (<99.0%) at 15% is acceptable.

If you can accept those two adjustments, we can move to final redlines and circulate to execs for signature. I'll attach our proposed redline doc (contract-redlines.docx) — the changes are limited to the Appendix A notice window and the first credit band percentage.

Would you like a short call to close these two bullets, or do you prefer to exchange a final redline? Either works for us.

Best,
